sentences.text: The genus name honors the ship HMS Bounty, which brought Europeans to the islands, and the food value the bird provided. The specific epithet obsoleta derives from the Latin adjective meaning "extinct" or "forgotten about".
Scientists described the species from 18 bones found at four archaeological sites on Henderson Island, primarily from early Polynesian middens.
Bountyphaps obsoleta was described in 2008 based on subfossil remains discovered on Henderson Island in the Pitcairn Group of southeastern Polynesia.
An indeterminate species, possibly the same as Bountyphaps obsoleta, has also been found in the Gambier archipelago.
While its affinities are uncertain, comparisons suggest Bountyphaps is most closely related to living species like the Nicobar pigeon or tooth-billed pigeon, and by extension, the dodo.
The species lived during the Holocene, from 0.0117 million years ago to 0 million years ago.
Bountyphaps became extinct following human colonization of Henderson Island, an event that occurred by 1050 CE.
